analysis.title: GS Esposito - US Flows Themes Mkts Macro Energy Breadth Flows Positioning Earnings Single Stocks Risk Views Week Ahead 5 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities were mixed last week: S&P 500 -0.27%, Nasdaq +0.45%, Russell 2000 -0.16%. Treasuries were mostly weaker with the curve steepening, and the 10Y and 30Y hit ~24-year yield highs before easing slightly on Friday.

September NFP printed +29k vs ~90k consensus, with -60k net two-month revisions and unemployment rising to 4.2%. Core PCE rose +0.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y, helped by methodological adjustments. October FOMC hike probability fell from 64% to below 25%.
NY Fed President Williams ('no urgency') and Vice Chair Jefferson ('judgment may take more time') also pushed down hike odds. GS Econ moved its second expected Fed hike from October to December.

WTI crude fell 1.40% on the week after a coordinated G7/IEA emergency release of up to 100m barrels of diesel and crude over 4 months. UKMTO confirmed 2 commercial crude tanker projectile strikes in and around the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend. Iran's Parliament Speaker said the waterway stays closed until Tehran's Memorandum conditions are met.

Market breadth is the weakest since the Dot Com Bubble. The S&P 500 is 2% from its ATH while the median stock is 17% below its ATH. RSP (equal weight) fell 70bps last week and has declined 7 straight weeks. Under 25% of S&P constituents closed above their 50-day moving average on Friday.

GS execution: US equities were modestly net bought on the week, driven by short covering in Macro Products and partly offset by continued shorting in Single Stocks. 8 of 11 sectors were net sold, led by Comm Svcs, Consumer Discretionary and Materials. Health Care was by far the most net bought, on short covering.

Energy is the most net sold US sector over the past month in $ and SD terms, almost entirely short sales, with HFs net selling the sector for 6 straight weeks even though oil is near multi-year highs.

GS Prime: Fundamental L/S gross leverage fell 1.7 pts to 206.2% (21st percentile 1-year) and net leverage fell 2.1 pts to 53.0% (7th percentile 1-year). GS Sentiment Indicator is -0.7 SD (vs -0.9 SD prior week). With single stocks net shorted for a 3rd straight week, GS frames the pain trade as an upside bleed higher.

Q3 earnings season starts next week, with 70% of S&P market cap reporting by month-end. Consensus expects 27% y/y S&P 500 EPS growth in Q3, vs 33% realized in Q2 excluding some accounting distortions. AI infrastructure beneficiaries account for over 50% of EPS growth, with hyperscaler capex growth of 116%.

Tech and Energy are expected to deliver y/y EPS growth of 64% and 109% and about 80% of total S&P 500 EPS growth. MU and NVDA together account for more than one-third of index growth. S&P forward P/E has compressed from 22.0x at the start of the cycle to 19.1x.

Single-stock moves: CCL +15.8% (beat, record 2027 booked occupancy and pricing), NKE -5.3% (weak guidance), STX -7.4% and WDC -9.1% (Nikkei report that Toshiba is investing to double HDD production in FY27), MDB -12.8% (CEO stepping down), ACN +12.7% (beat and raise), SNPS +15.1% (multiyear IP agreement with AMZN), MAT +14.9% (takeover interest from Authentic Brands), HPE +10.2% (raised FY27 Networking guidance), CBOE +5.1% (25-year index licensing extension), CAG -6.7%, FICO -23.4% (FHFA regulatory headlines).

Rich Privorotsky (GS EU Eq Trading) says positioning is extremely light, macro shorts are large and Russell positioning is near the bottom of its recent range, so the market likely bleeds higher. He calls energy the key tail, says French/European sovereign risk is harder to dismiss, and expects very good earnings. His view changes if sentiment turns euphoric or positioning gets stretched.

Week ahead: ISM Services Monday (GS expects 55.4), trade balance Tuesday (GS -$100.0bn, consensus -$102.0bn, last -$88.6bn), FOMC minutes Wednesday. Earnings: RPM, LW, APOG, STZ Tuesday, LEVI and APLD Wednesday, PEP, ANGO, TLRY Thursday, DAL Friday. MRVL and ZS hold analyst/investor days.

GS Econ (Hatzius): August core PCE rose 0.25% m/m and 3.01% y/y, both below expectations, with benchmark revisions driven largely by portfolio management costs. The 2026 Q4/Q4 core PCE forecast is cut to 3.0% vs the median FOMC participant at 3.4%. GS sees a growing chance that no more hikes are needed.
Q2 GDP was revised up to +2.2% annualised, with consumer spending +3.8% and investment +4.6%. A wider August trade deficit led GS to trim Q3 GDP tracking to +3.3%.

US Strategy (Snider): Q3 consensus EPS growth of 27% is the strongest pre-season expectation since 2021. Cloud revenue growth is forecast to accelerate from 48% to 55%. Only 2% of S&P 500 companies quantified an earnings benefit from AI last quarter.

Global equity funds had net inflows of +$16bn in the week to September 30 (vs -$10bn prior week), with technology funds the largest inflows and US funds still in outflow. Money market fund assets fell $118bn.

GS PB: Fundamental L/S performance was -0.45% from 9/25 to 10/1 (MSCI World TR -0.67%), mostly beta. Systematic L/S rose +1.14% on +1.27% alpha. Overall gross leverage was unchanged at 308.0% (55th percentile) and net at 77.4% (29th percentile). Global equities were net bought +0.7 SD, with long buys outpacing short sales 2.7 to 1.

Health Care saw the largest % net buying by HFs in over 6 months, from North America short covers and European long buys. The Prime book is +5.5% overweight Health Care vs MSCI World (46th percentile 1-year, 89th percentile 5-year).
Semis (Schneider): the best 3Q setup since the correction. Highest-conviction names are AMAT, MCHP, STX, LRCX, ONTO, TER, AMD and SITM. More cautious on QCOM, KLAC, WDC, TXN, ARM, ENTG and MKSI.

Banks (Ramsden): NII is the key earnings driver, supported by 7-9% loan growth, fixed-rate asset repricing and a steeper curve. Highest-conviction ideas are WFC, BAC and C. Valuations are ~11x FY+2 EPS, ~60% of the S&P 500 multiple.
GIR October Conviction List adds AMZN, BURL, HII, JCI and OXY. JCI data center cooling backlog is a record $21bn (+32% organic in F3Q26), with organic orders up over 30% for 3 straight quarters.

Neil Mehta upgraded OXY to Buy (PT $69) on enhanced oil recovery, debt reduction from ~$29bn to ~$11.8bn, and a ~14% average 2027/28 FCF yield. He downgraded TOU to Sell (PT $49) on weak AECO gas prices and elevated storage, preferring AR.
